## Upgrading to 5.14

### Server

- Static files are sent with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, no longer with the four weeks of tiles. Their URLs stay the same when the files change, so after a frontend update a browser kept its old scripts for up to four weeks and showed a half-updated page. Now it checks every time, and an unchanged file costs an empty `304`. `server.cache_control` and `--cache-control` apply only to tiles and `tiles.json`. To keep static files cached for longer, set `cache_control` on their `static` entry in the configuration file. Behind a CDN, `no-cache` means more conditional requests reach the server.
- Node.js: `addStaticSource()` takes the header as an optional third argument, and the `cacheControl` option of `TileServer` no longer applies to static files.
- Rust: `StaticSourceConfig` has the new field `cache_control`, and `TileServer::add_static_source_config` mounts one with it.

### VPL

- `from_gdal_dem` marks pixels without a height as transparent: outside the dataset, outside the cutline, and on the dataset's `nodata` value. Tiles at the edge of the data now carry an alpha channel, and tiles without any data are left out. Tiles the data covers completely are unchanged. Transparent pixels have the colour of 0 m, so a reader that ignores alpha sees what it saw before at the edge of the data, and 0 m in a void, where it used to see -10000 m.
